As a Financial Analyst, GTM, you’ll:

 - Own the GTM expense plan and forecast, covering headcount and non-headcount spend, and turn it into executive-ready commentary for Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders on variances, risks, and investment tradeoffs

 - Manage GTM headcount planning and capacity, including hiring plans, ratios such as quota-carrying reps to sales support, and attrition, and flag drift from targets before it affects the forecast

 - Reduce manual effort in planning by improving Workday and Adaptive Planning workflows, removing manual tagging, and setting materiality thresholds so non-headcount forecast updates focus on spend that moves the outlook

 - Own the single source of truth for ARR and ATR across our Sales and Self-Serve models, auditing the ARR in Salesforce and the data warehouse, documenting metric definitions, and resolving breaks with Revenue Operations, Data and/or Accounting

 - Run the monthly churn, renewal, and write-off review with GTM partners, preparing the analysis, root-cause commentary, and forecast implications leaders use to make decisions

 - Synthesize multi-source data from Salesforce, the data warehouse, Workday, and NetSuite into clear metrics, KPIs, and business narratives that inform GTM leadership decisions

 - Build working relationships across Finance, Accounting, Procurement, and GTM to drive alignment without formal authority, and automate recurring reporting with SQL, spreadsheets, and AI tools

 - BS / BA college degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field, or relevant experience

 - Have a working understanding of SaaS metrics such as ARR, NRR, GRR, churn, and renewals, and can trace them back to source data in Salesforce and the data warehouse

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

 An overview of this role 
 As an Intermediate Backend Engineer (Python) in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers the reusable building blocks agents and flows are made from as well as our core harness, Duo Developer.
 Most of your work will be backend engineering in Python, using libraries such as LangGraph to build secure, reliable and scalable features in our AI Gateway. You'll also work across the stack where needed. You'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.
 What you'll do 
 Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the Duo Workflow Service, the AI Gateway and, where needed, the GitLab monolith. Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.
 Build and improve agentic flows and their reusable parts with LangChain and LangGraph, including the Flow Registry.
 Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.
 Design, implement and review APIs (including GraphQL and REST) and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients such as the GitLab monolith, IDE extensions and Duo CLI.
 Improve and extend automated testing (pytest and other frameworks), including evaluations of agent and flow behavior, to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.
 Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.
 Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.
 Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class as more work becomes agentic.
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience building and maintaining production Python backend applications, including APIs, asynchronous or background processing, and data models.
 Experience with LLM application frameworks such as LangGraph, or designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or harnesses.
 Skill in designing or extending APIs (REST, GraphQL or gRPC) with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.
 Comfort working across the stack in a mature codebase. Familiarity with Ruby on Rails and/or JavaScript and Vue is a plus.
 Experience finding and fixing performance bottlenecks in applications.
 Clear written and verbal communication, including technical proposals and documentation, in a remote, async, cross-functional team.
 Openness to learning and to applying skills from related technologies or fields.
 About the team 
 The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. We provide the platform, catalog and execution features that help teams deliver resilient agents and flows to customers. The stage has three groups: Agent Developer, AI Catalog and Agent Execution. Between them, they own the GitLab Duo Developer foundational flow and the Flow Registry; the AI Catalog, including custom agents, custom flows and external agent integrations; and agent execution, agent tools and agent observability.
 Our engineers work async-first across EMEA, AMER, and India timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

As a member of Ramp's Fraud Operations team, you will play a pivotal role in safeguarding the company and its customers against fraudulent activities. This position involves analyzing new account applications, monetary and non-monetary account activity to identify and mitigate risks associated with first-party and third-party fraud.

We are seeking a detail-oriented professional who is adept at applying fraud detection techniques and leveraging data sources and tools to develop logical courses of action. In addition to technical acumen, this role requires strong interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively cross-functionally and with customers, external financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies. Ideal candidates are self-starters who are energized by ambiguity and love creating clarity.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Analyze new account applications to detect potential fraud patterns, including identity theft, synthetic identities, and other high-risk behaviors.

 - Evaluate transactional activity, identifying anomalies and irregularities indicative of fraudulent behavior.

 - Thoroughly investigate alerts of first-party and third-party fraud, providing comprehensive documentation of findings.

 - Investigate and facilitate customer card disputes, ensuring cases are resolved accurately and within network timelines.

 - Use AI tools and automation to streamline investigations, and help develop and improve the processes and tooling behind them.

 - Collaborate with internal teams, such as Credit Risk, Compliance, and Customer Support, to ensure timely resolution of fraud-related issues.

 - Communicate directly with customers to verify account activity, resolve disputes, and gather necessary documentation during investigations.

 - Liaise with external stakeholders, including financial institutions and law enforcement, to support investigations and facilitate recovery efforts when necessary.

 This is an exciting opportunity to join The Care Company as we continue to build and expand our Occupational Therapy program .  An Occupational Therapist looking to supplement your existing caseload or practice.

 Looking for greater flexibility and autonomy over your schedule.
 Passionate about helping clients remain safe and independent in their homes.

 Complete comprehensive in-home assessments within the required referral timeframe, including functional assessments, mobility evaluations, falls risk assessments, equipment needs, and ADL/IADL evaluations.

The short version
 Every order Portless ships moves money in two directions. We bill merchants for shipping, fulfillment, storage, duties and taxes, and we pay carriers, warehouses and partners across several countries and currencies. Our P&L sits in the middle.
 We've grown fast, and we're investing in the systems behind that money flow to match. We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own it end to end: from rate card to invoice to cash, and from carrier bill to audited cost.
 About Portless
 Portless is changing the face of global e-commerce. By decoupling brands from traditional, expensive domestic warehousing, we let e-commerce companies ship directly from manufacturing hubs to global consumers in as little as three to five days.
 We move packages to 75+ countries for hundreds of DTC brands, with millions of packages shipped annually, 99.8% pick-and-pack accuracy, and 98% on-time delivery. We're a small, remote-first team growing fast, and the work you do here shows up in a merchant's business, and on our own books, within weeks.
 What you'll own
 We're building out our finance infrastructure for the next stage of growth. You'll set the product direction for:
 Billing (order to cash). Rate cards, pricing rules, invoicing, disputes and collections. You'll own our billing engine from the product side, including rolling it out across our merchant base.
 Cost audit (procure to pay). Ingesting carrier and partner invoices, matching them to what we shipped, and catching discrepancies automatically.
 Margin visibility. A shipment-level view of revenue, cost and pass-through charges that finance and leadership can rely on.
 Duties and taxes. How tariffs, VAT and other pass-through charges are calculated, billed and collected, in close partnership with our compliance team.
 The merchant experience. How merchants see, understand and ask questions about their charges.
 You'll be the bridge between finance, operations and engineering, turning finance needs into a clear roadmap.
 What success looks like
 First 90 days
 An end-to-end view of how money moves through Portless today, and a clear picture of where it needs to go
 A finance product strategy and sequenced roadmap, aligned with finance, operations and engineering
 Priorities set and defended in writing, with the reasoning and tradeoffs behind them
 First 6 months
 Most merchants billed automatically and on time
 Our largest carriers' invoices matched and audited automatically
 Finance can see margin by shipment, merchant and lane
 Measurable time given back to the finance and CS teams
 What we're looking for
 Product craft first. This is the bar we're least flexible on.
 5+ years in product management owning a complex, data-heavy domain
 You can map a messy process to where data originates, where it breaks, and where the leverage is
 You get your own answers with SQL or AI tools, and check claims against what actually happened
 You ship what works this quarter while building toward the right end state, and you write it up clearly
 Finance and logistics experience.
 You've built product for billing, AP, carrier audit, payments or financial infrastructure, ideally in logistics, freight or fulfillment
 You're fluent in rate cards, accruals, pass-through vs. revenue, invoice matching, and how operational data reaches the GL
 You work closely with accountants and finance ops and know when to bring in the CFO. This isn't an accounting role
 Exposure to duties, tariffs or VAT is a strong plus
 How you work.
 Forward-deployed: close to finance, our China operations and merchants, with evening calls and potential travel to China
 You work off one canonical roadmap alongside the rest of product
 You partner across finance, engineering, operations, CS, compliance and merchants
 You look for the systemic version of the problem

 About CO280 
 CO280 is a leading developer of low-carbon industrial infrastructure projects. As a top 3 global BECCS developer, we hold more than $1B in signed CDR offtakes from buyers including Microsoft, Google, JPMorgan, Salesforce, and Stripe. We pioneered BECCS in North America, partnering with the continent's largest pulp and paper companies to retrofit mills with carbon capture and sequestration and deliver permanent carbon removal at scale. 
 We are now expanding to deliver low-carbon power solutions across the data center market, applying key advantages we already possess: trusted hyperscaler relationships, a portfolio of pre-qualified industrial sites, expertise in energy and CCS project development and access to capital. We've identified and pre-qualified more than 20 industrial sites representing approximately 6 GW of potential capacity — not just parcels of land, but strategic infrastructure platforms with existing industrial zoning, water rights, transmission access, and established host relationships that dramatically compress development timelines in a market where speed-to-power is everything. 
 This is the rare moment when a market this large is gated by a problem this specific. The AI buildout is the defining industrial expansion of the decade, and power is the constraint holding it back, with interconnection queues running four to seven years and the industry defaulting to unabated gas it does not want to burn. CO280 is building the platform that answers it.  
 You'll join a close-knit team of entrepreneurial, collaborative, and transparent operators who have developed, delivered, and scaled new technologies and industrial infrastructure across multiple verticals.  We believe clean power must be practical, bankable, and scalable to move the needle on net zero and earn social license. If you want to help build the projects the energy transition is waiting on, this is a seat at the table. 
 The Role 
 The Vice President Project Development will build and lead CO280's low carbon power data center infrastructure platform — owning project origination, development strategy, strategic partnerships, and the project development organization. You will identify, originate, secure, and advance gigawatt-scale infrastructure opportunities from concept through Final Investment Decision (FID), working across utilities, industrial hosts, OEMs, EPCs, hyperscalers, AI developers, and capital partners to turn strategic sites into bankable projects. 
 This is a relationship-driven leadership role. Success will depend as much on the executive relationships you bring as the projects you've delivered. Existing relationships across hyperscalers, neoclouds, data center developers, utilities, power developers, OEMs, EPCs, infrastructure investors, and other strategic partners will enable CO280 to originate opportunities faster and build projects that competitors cannot. 
 Solutions may span gas-to-power + CCS, biomass, and solar with storage — owned and operated by CO280 and/or with partners. You own development through FID; at FID, the project engineering team leads execution, with your continued commercial support through construction to commercial operation. 
 This role exists because the AI industry has discovered that compute is no longer constrained by chips — it's constrained by power. Every major hyperscaler is competing to secure gigawatts of generation capacity while utilities face interconnection queues measured in years. CO280 is uniquely positioned to solve that problem by combining strategic industrial sites, deep customer relationships, and proven infrastructure development expertise. The Vice President Project Development will convert those advantages into one of North America's largest low-carbon infrastructure portfolios. 
 Your first 12–18 months will include: 
 Building CO280's project development function and playbook. 
 Converting pre-qualified host sites into data center-ready opportunities. 
 Securing the company's first anchor AI infrastructure customers. 
 Advancing the first one or two projects to Final Investment Decision. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Origination & Development 
 Drive new low-carbon power projects from origination through FID, then support the project engineering team commercially through construction to commercial operation. 
 Develop CO280's project origination strategy by matching industrial host sites with hyperscaler demand, transmission availability, fiber infrastructure and regional power market opportunities. 
 Own the development budget and project economics for each project through stage-gates to FID, including scenario and sensitivity analysis on key inputs. 
 Partnerships & Commercial 
 Build executive relationships with utilities, industrial hosts, hyperscalers, neoclouds, data center developers, OEMs, EPCs, gas suppliers, and strategic partners across the project value chain. 
 Negotiate contracts with project partners, working closely with project engineering, finance, legal, community engagement, and commercial teams. 
 Partner with the commercial team to map the hyperscaler and AI-buyer channel end-to-end, translating buyer needs directly into project design and the development roadmap. 
 Cross-Functional Delivery 
 Partner with engineering to develop technically robust, commercially attractive, and financeable projects, including coordinating studies, and building relationships with OEM and EPC partners. 
 Align with finance to ensure projects are bankable, supporting project economic models and corporate/project financing activities. 
 Manage the operating cadence — stage-gates, risk registers, development-budget discipline, and project economic performance. 
 Leadership & Strategy

 Shape CO280's long-term infrastructure strategy as a member of the executive leadership team, defining where the business plays, how it wins, and how it scales.

 This is an opportunity to build one of North America's leading AI infrastructure development platforms at the point where energy, industrial redevelopment and hyperscale computing converge. 
 Location

 At least 30% travel across North America 
 Qualifications

 The entrepreneurial mindset to build a new business in a rapidly evolving market.

Vous êtes chef de cuisine et vous rêvez de travailler au Québec ? 
 Vous cherchez une cuisine où vous avez enfin la main sur la carte, une petite équipe, et un cadre qui donne envie de se lever le matin. Ça tombe bien. 
 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un endroit où on a envie de travailler tous les jours.
 Ici, c'est une auberge-restaurant installée dans une maison ancestrale, sur la Côte-de-Beaupré, face au fleuve Saint-Laurent. Vingt minutes de Québec, dix minutes du Mont-Sainte-Anne. Huit chambres rénovées à l'étage, un restaurant au rez-de-chaussée, et une réputation solide auprès des gens du coin comme des touristes qui viennent de France, des États-Unis et de partout au Canada.
 On y sert entre 35 et 50 couverts sur un service classique, et plus de 100 quand il y a un mariage ou un événement. L'été, ça tourne fort. Le reste de l'année, la clientèle locale prend le relais, avec le brunch du dimanche qui est une institution.
 L'entreprise compte 23 personnes, dont une brigade de cuisine de 5 au maximum. Autant dire qu'on se connaît tous, et que le patron est joignable directement.
 Votre rôle 
 Vous prenez la direction de la cuisine. La production quotidienne, l'équipe, les commandes, et surtout la carte.

À côté, vous avez la main libre pour développer une carte plus contemporaine, avec vos influences — cuisine québécoise moderne, italienne, française.  The Opportunity 
 If you are an exceptional researcher and writer who enjoys learning about new industries, solving problems and turning complex information into a compelling business case, this role may be an excellent fit.  researching and developing the written content required for government funding applications.

 Research & Grant Application Development 
 Research clients, industries, technologies, equipment, production processes, markets and other technical or business topics required to develop strong funding applications.

 Partner closely with Funding Specialists to understand each client's business, proposed project, and overall funding strategy.

 Government Funding Research 
 Research new and existing government funding programs across Canada and the United States. 
 Interpret complex program guidelines and translate them into practical eligibility requirements, funding considerations, and application strategies. 
 Identify programs that may align with existing client projects and communicate potential opportunities to the broader team. 
 Stay informed about government priorities, economic developments, emerging industries and business trends that may influence funding opportunities. 
 Contribute research and program intelligence to BDO GrantMatch's internal funding knowledge base and proprietary technology platform.

 Develop and maintain realistic workback schedules in collaboration with Funding Specialists.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

ABOUT US
 We're a fast-growing group within Valsoft Corporation, working where payments meet AI. The group includes ValPay, TNRM, P&P and Sadie.
 Sadie is the #1 voice AI reservation platform in the world, with customers in Australia, Europe, the United States and Canada.
 ValPay is a payment facilitator (payfac). In plain terms, it lets other businesses accept and process payments through ValPay's own merchant infrastructure. That means they can start taking payments quickly, without setting up their own costly merchant account that can take a long time to get approved. ValPay is one of the fastest-growing companies in Canada.
 Our growth has been recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50, and we've reached a turning point. We've outgrown a traditional startup finance function, and we're building what comes next: a leaner, more technical, more automated finance team designed for how a modern payments and AI business really works. We don't want to copy how larger, slower companies do finance.
 ABOUT THE ROLE 
 This role is a rare chance to help build a finance function where accounting and technology meet. Our finance setup dates from our startup days, and we're rebuilding it to match the pace and complexity of the business.
 As Senior Controller, you'll own revenue recognition and technical accounting across multiple entities. Just as important, you'll have real, hands-on ownership of the automation and data work that more and more of our finance function runs on.
 This role is ideal for a CPA who's ready to grow beyond traditional accounting and specialize in accounting and technology together. You don't need deep AI or automation experience. What matters most is a strong accounting foundation and the drive to build that expertise.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 
 Own revenue recognition and every judgmental or complex accounting entry across all entities, including usage-based and payfac revenue under IFRS
 Review and approve accounting entries across the group
 Set technical accounting policy for the group, and make sure it's applied consistently across entities in different jurisdictions
 Own and keep improving the group's core processes and controls across multiple entities and currencies, and build scalable, well-documented processes as we grow
 Lead the multi-entity close and consolidation
 Take a hands-on role in building the automation and data infrastructure that connects usage, billing and payment-settlement data across the group. As the function matures, you'll have a real chance to build deep expertise in financial systems and data modeling.
 Build your skills with AI tools in day-to-day work such as journal entry review, reconciliation and reporting, with the goal of making them central to how you work
 Manage and review the work of the Controller and transactional support staff, bringing organization, structure and focus to a team we're building from the ground up
 Be the main escalation point for technical accounting questions, taking over this role from the CFO
 Work directly with our international tax specialist and external auditors on statutory filings, transfer pricing and audit requirements across our four entities
 WHAT YOU'LL BRING 
 CPA designation (or equivalent international designation)
 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of technical accounting
 Solid understanding of IFRS
 Experience closing and consolidating financials across multiple legal entities and/or jurisdictions
 Experience reviewing and managing the work of other accounting staff, either as a people leader or through strong review and mentoring
 Curiosity about data, systems and automation, and a drive to get fluent in them. Hands-on experience with AI tools or data modeling is a plus, not a requirement.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll work directly with the CFO, the auditors and, as the team grows, other finance staff.
 Comfort in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment that calls for significant hands-on work
 NICE TO HAVE 
 Exposure to finance automation, RPA or AI-assisted accounting tools
 Experience in payments or payment facilitation
 An audit background at a Big 4 or national fir
 Experience in a multi-entity, PE-backed or acquisitive group
 French proficiency (our team is based in Montreal)
 WHAT WE OFFER 
 A clear growth path: you can specialize in accounting and technology as the function matures, working closely with the CFO along the way
 Cross-border work: you'll work directly with an international tax specialist on cross-border and transfer pricing matters
 A strong team: a close-knit finance team inside a high-growth company recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50
 Real impact: a high-ownership, in-office culture where your technical and automation work directly shapes how finance scales
_____________________________________________________________________________________
 À PROPOS DE NOUS 
 Nous sommes un groupe en forte croissance au sein de Valsoft Corporation, à la croisée des paiements et de l'intelligence artificielle. Le groupe comprend ValPay, TNRM, P&P et Sadie.
 Sadie est la plateforme de réservation par IA vocale no 1 au monde, avec des clients en Australie, en Europe, aux États-Unis et au Canada.

Ces entreprises peuvent ainsi commencer à accepter des paiements rapidement, sans avoir à ouvrir leur propre compte marchand, une démarche coûteuse et souvent longue à faire approuver. ValPay est l'une des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide au Canada.

Notre fonction finance a dépassé le modèle traditionnel d'une jeune entreprise, et nous bâtissons la suite : une équipe finance plus agile, plus technique et plus automatisée, conçue pour le fonctionnement réel d'une entreprise moderne de paiements et d'IA. Nous ne voulons pas reproduire la façon de faire des grandes entreprises plus lentes.

Cyclic Materials is building a resilient circular supply chain for rare earth elements and other critical materials. Through our fully integrated proprietary technology platform, we recover rare earths from end-of-life products and transform them into high-purity materials used to produce new permanent magnets. These magnets are critical to the modern economy, underpinning AI, automotive, e-mobility, electronics, semiconductor, energy, defense, and other advanced manufacturing sectors.
Founded in 2021, Cyclic Materials has rapidly become a category leader in rare earth recovery, achieving commercial operations in less than five years. We currently operate facilities in Ontario and Arizona, with further expansion underway in South Carolina. Backed by investment accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., alongside strategic investors including Microsoft, Amazon, Hitachi Ventures, BMW i Ventures, Jaguar Land Rover’s InMotion fund, Energy Impact Partners, ArcTern Ventures, and Fifth Wall, we are scaling quickly and building the industrial backbone required to meet growing global demand for a secure and sustainable supply of rare earths.
We have established an extensive and growing network of commercial partnerships with global industry leaders such as Solvay, Vattenfall, Lime, and VACUUMSCHMELZE, enabling the rapid deployment of recycled rare earth materials into real-world supply chains. Joining Cyclic Materials means tackling complex and exciting challenges at scale alongside a team committed to strong execution and measurable impact. If you are motivated by building critical infrastructure and advancing the circular economy, join us and help accelerate the growth of rare earth recycling.
 JOB DESCRIPTION
 As a Scientist on the R & D team, you will focus on developing new approaches and sustainable recycling process steps for converting rare earth containing waste into valuable products. Your role will be dedicated to expanding Cyclic Materials’ capabilities, including work in metallization of REEs and supporting ongoing projects. The ideal candidate will be responsible for the development, optimization, and implementation of metallization processes for rare earth metals and alloys. This role plays a crucial part in advancing our capabilities in material science, particularly in the application of rare earth materials for electronic, aerospace, energy, and other high-performance industries. Most of your time will be spent in the lab performing experiments and characterizing products and raw materials. This is a full-time, hybrid role based in Kingston, ON. This is a great opportunity for someone who thrives in a hands-on, fast-paced environment and is excited to make a meaningful impact.
 Key Responsibilities:
 Review of existing metallization technologies for rare earths and come up with new innovative ideas
 Design, develop, and optimize metallization techniques for rare earth elements and alloys
 Design, setup, and perform novel experiments to test and define new process steps
 Perform standardized bench-scale experiments to evaluate materials and process parameters
 Prepare standard reports, presentations, and summarize experimental results clearly and concisely to other team members
 Support ongoing operations, R&D test work and Cyclic goals as needed
 Qualifications:
 Bachelor's/Master’s/Doctorate degree in any stream aligned with the job requirements
 At least 3 years of proven experience in the metallization (Carbothermic Reduction or Molten salt electrolysis) of rare earths, titanium, zirconium, niobium, and tantalum.
 Knowledge and direct experience with electrochemical and metallothermic methods for metal reduction
 Experience with fluorination and chlorination of rare earth oxides
 Capable of designing and conducting metal refining processes such as vacuum distillation, zone refining and electrorefining
 Excellent knowledge of pyrometallurgical and electrometallurgical processes
 Demonstrated ability to analyze experimental data, reach conclusions, and communicate results
 Excellent knowledge of software for phase diagrams and other thermodynamic calculations (FactSage, Thermo-Calc, etc.)
 Familiarity with chemical engineering (e.g., mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, transport phenomena) and electrochemistry principles (e.g., charge transfer, Current-Voltage relationships)
 Candidates with extensive industrial experience on metallization are welcome to apply in lieu of above-mentioned qualifications
 The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively as needed
 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
 Preferred Qualifications:
 A safety-first mindset: share potential risks with others before they result in hazardous outcomes
 Knowledge of milling, and physical separation methods is an asset
 Experience or the desire to be in a dynamic startup environment
 A critical thinking mindset and focus on finding answers
 A desire to challenge yourself and take on increasing responsibilities as the company grows
 Pay Range

 References from sales managers or business owners you’ve closed for.
